title: Survey KV-cache & memory tiering for $/token
spec:
Objective: Map techniques that reduce GPU memory pressure and $/token for LLM serving via KV-cache management (PagedAttention follow-ons, prefix caching, KV compression/quantization, CPU/disk offload, hierarchical cache).

Output format:
1) Markdown artifact `survey/kv-memory-tiering.md` (≤4k words) with sections: techniques, vLLM baseline comparison, cost model variables, workload sensitivity.
2) `hypothesis_propose` 1–2 concrete hosting approaches (title + claim + evidence URLs).
3) `board_post` channel=findings kind=finding summary + @orchestrator.

Sources/tools: WebSearch; cite vLLM docs, PagedAttention paper, recent KV offload papers (e.g. FlexGen, CacheBlend, Mooncake/KV-centric systems if relevant), industry blog posts with benchmarks.

Boundaries: Do NOT implement code. Do NOT claim GPU measurements. Do NOT clone repos. Focus on cost-per-token mechanism, not raw TFLOPS.
resultMd: Delivered survey/kv-memory-tiering.md (artifact sar_F8vemRPU_Xf_, ~12.5KB): techniques (PagedAttention/APC, FP8/KIVI compression, vLLM offload, LMCache, Mooncake, CacheBlend, FlexGen, py-kvcache), vLLM baseline comparison, cost-model variables for 512/128 default, workload sensitivity matrix, ranked ideas, prototype sketch. Proposed 2 hypotheses: FP8-resident KV concurrency; break-even gated cluster KV pool. Posted #findings summary with primary URLs. No code, no fabricated GPU benchmarks; estimates labeled.

title: Survey disaggregated prefill/decode serving
spec:
Objective: Analyze disaggregated LLM serving (separate prefill and decode workers, network transfer of KV, autoscaling per phase) for cost-per-token vs monolithic vLLM.

Output format:
1) Artifact `survey/disaggregated-serving.md` covering Splitwise/DistServe-class designs, transfer costs, hardware sizing, failure modes.
2) 1–2 `hypothesis_propose` entries with quantified *estimated* savings ranges and cited sources.
3) findings post on board.

Sources: Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, TetriInfer, prefill-decode disaggregation papers/blogs; cloud networking cost assumptions (label estimates).

Boundaries: No code. No fabricated paper titles. Compare fairly to continuous batching vLLM baseline. Do not assume infinite network bandwidth.
resultMd:
Delivered artifact `survey/disaggregated-serving.md` (~13KB): Splitwise, DistServe, TetriInfer, Mooncake, vLLM/Meta P/D; KV transfer economics with cited formulas; hardware sizing; failure modes; fair vLLM continuous-batching comparison; ESTIMATE $/token scenarios for 512/128 chat.

Proposed 2 hypotheses: (1) heterogeneous H100 prefill + A100 decode — ESTIMATE 25–45% $/token vs homogeneous vLLM; (2) SLO-goodput P/D — ESTIMATE 30–75% $/token vs vLLM at 512+ prompts.

Posted finding to #findings with primary URLs (Splitwise arXiv, DistServe OSDI, TetriInfer, Mooncake, vLLM disagg docs).

title: Survey batching, scheduling & speculative decoding
spec:
Objective: Identify batching/scheduling and speculative/cascade decoding methods that improve effective tokens/$ (utilization, fewer full forward passes, draft model economics).

Output format:
1) Artifact `survey/batching-speculative.md` (continuous batching limits, chunk prefill, SLA-aware schedulers, Medusa/Eagle/speculative decoding, model cascades).
2) 1–2 hypotheses proposing novel or combined hosting stacks.
3) findings board post.

Sources: vLLM scheduling docs, Orca/ SARATHI papers, speculative decoding literature, production blog benchmarks.

Boundaries: No GPU benchmarks in this env. Separate latency vs cost tradeoffs. Do not conflate throughput-only wins with $/token wins.
resultMd:
Delivered survey/batching-speculative.md (~12KB) covering Orca continuous batching, Sarathi/Sarathi-Serve chunked prefill & stall-free scheduling, vLLM scheduler knobs & spec-decode methods, Leviathan/Medusa/EAGLE/MTP/FrugalGPT cascades, ranked tokens/$ mapping, and three prototype sketches.

Primary sources: Orca OSDI'22, Sarathi arXiv:2308.16369, Sarathi-Serve OSDI'24, vLLM optimization & spec decode docs, Leviathan ICML'23, Medusa ICML'24, EAGLE arXiv:2401.15077, FrugalGPT arXiv:2305.05176, QLM arXiv:2407.00047, Llumnix OSDI'24.

Hypotheses: sh_KrYdzqNouLeB (layered spec + Sarathi-Serve on single fleet, ESTIMATE 1.4–2.2× $/token); sh_ddcnRBuw2Qzp (FrugalGPT gateway + spec target pool, ESTIMATE 2–4× $/token for routable chat mixes).

Board: finding sp__N90EuMr2DOm on #findings. No GPU measurements.

title: Critique incoming hosting hypotheses
spec:
Objective: As researchers post hypotheses, produce rigorous critiques (hidden costs, workload mismatch, evidence gaps, vLLM feature overlap).

Output format: For each hypothesis reviewed: `board_post` channel=findings kind=critique referencing hypothesis id; update hypothesis critique count via substantive challenge (≥150 words each). Target ≥4 hypotheses critiqued before synthesizer runs.

Sources: Same papers as researchers; cross-check claims against cited URLs.

Boundaries: Do not propose new full architectures (short alternatives OK). Do not block on perfect data — flag uncertainty. No ad hominem.
resultMd: Critiqued all 6 hypotheses (≥150 words each via hypothesis_critique + #findings board_post): sh_Q5ZdrV1rxF5u (5, needs_evidence — vLLM FP8 flag = baseline hygiene not novel host); sh_MbLTga-xgKid (6, conditional outer layer); sh_sYDvYqohPgEc (7, true heterogeneous P/D topology); sh_V2irZVB1OP99 (7, DistServe goodput story strongest disagg); sh_KrYdzqNouLeB (4, refute multiplicative 1.4–2.2× $/token); sh_ddcnRBuw2Qzp (6, cascade vs always-large not vs tuned single-model vLLM). Verified primary citation URLs. Flagged fair baseline = FP8+APC vLLM per orchestrator directive.

title: Synthesize report + prototype architecture
spec:
Objective: Produce the swarm final report ranking hosting approaches vs vLLM* on $/token and a concrete prototype design.

Output format:
1) artifact `report.md` kind=report (≤8k words): executive summary, vLLM* baseline definition, survey synthesis, ranked recommendations (top 3), risks, workload sensitivity, prototype section.
2) artifact `design/prototype-composite-pd.md` kind=design with components, data flows, admission policies, ESTIMATE cost model worked example (512/128 default).
3) board_post findings summary @orchestrator.

Sources: All survey/* artifacts, ranking/cost-per-token-rubric.md, hypothesis_list + critiques on board. Lead with composite sh_lphBfIh_oTE2 if critiques support; demote config-only (FP8-only) and FrugalGPT cascade if off-mission vs self-hosted vLLM*.

Boundaries: No code. Label ESTIMATE. Cite URLs. Do not declare_done.
resultMd:
Delivered synthesis artifacts:

1. **report.md** (sar_cxqve8Z-QQjJ, kind=report) — executive summary, vLLM* baseline, survey synthesis, ranked hypotheses with Elo + @cost-critic verdicts, ESTIMATE cost model, risks, experiments, build plan. Recommends **sh_lphBfIh_oTE2** composite P/D; demotes **sh_ddcnRBuw2Qzp** (FrugalGPT — API/multi-model scope) and **sh_Q5ZdrV1rxF5u** (FP8-only — vLLM* hygiene). Notes pending critique on composite.

2. **design/prototype-composite-pd.md** (sar_IXxGu1CfZNVV, kind=design) — components, data flows, L* admission, failure modes, worked 512/128 $/token example vs vLLM* (~$44 vs ~$28–39/1M tokens depending on η assumption).

3. **#findings** summary posted @orchestrator.

Sources: survey/*, ranking/cost-per-token-rubric.md, board critiques, hypothesis_list, orchestrator vLLM* decision sp_9SVWCozweWed.

title: Build cost-per-token ranking rubric
spec:
Objective: Define a reproducible rubric to compare hosting hypotheses on cost per token (and note latency/quality constraints).

Output format:
1) Artifact `ranking/cost-per-token-rubric.md` with formula: $/token = f(GPU/CPU $/hr, utilization, tokens/sec, overhead, storage/network).
2) Default scenario table (7B/70B, 1k concurrent, 512 in / 128 out) — all numbers labeled ESTIMATE.
3) Tournament rules: how to score pairwise matchups for `hypothesis_list` Elo.
4) Post decision-quality summary to #decisions.

Sources: Public cloud pricing pages (AWS/GCP list prices), published serving benchmarks.

Boundaries: Do not rank until ≥2 hypotheses exist — but deliver rubric now. Do not declare a winner without critic input.
resultMd: Delivered artifact `ranking/cost-per-token-rubric.md` (sar_sP-6wKBv4-tC): $/token = C_hour/(λ×(L_in+L_out)×3600) with compute/storage/network terms; default 512/128 chat scenario for 7B/70B @ ~1k concurrent with ESTIMATE list pricing ($12 H100, $4 A100 GPU-hr); tournament pairing/judging rules aligned to orchestrator novelty bar. Started Elo tournament on 6 live hypotheses — 6 record_match calls. Leaderboard: FrugalGPT cascade 1231, heterogeneous P/D & SLO-goodput P/D 1216 (drawn head-to-head), Sarathi+spec 1199, FP8 KV & gated KV pool 1169. Posted decision summary to #decisions with rubric refs and primary URLs.

title: Verify report claims and sources
spec:
Objective: Verify latest report.md artifact: URL validity, quote accuracy, ESTIMATE labels, fair vLLM* baseline, no fabricated numbers.

Output: artifact verify/verify-result.json with pass/fail, issue list; board_post findings kind=finding @orchestrator.

Boundaries: Blocked until report.md exists. Do not rewrite report—only verify.
resultMd: Verified report.md (sar_cxqve8Z-QQjJ): conditional PASS via verify_result. Published verify/verify-result.json; spot-checked 14 URLs and 6 headline claims (Splitwise, DistServe, Sarathi, FP8 54%, py-kvcache, analytic $/token ESTIMATEs). No fabricated claims. Issues: wrong FrugalGPT link labeled vLLM spec decode; stale pending-composite-critique text (critique now 7/10). design/prototype-composite-pd.md present. Findings posted to #findings @orchestrator.

title: Scan alternative stacks (CPU, serverless, edge)
spec:
Objective: Survey non-GPU-centric or heterogeneous hosting (llama.cpp/CPU, serverless GPU, multi-tenant L40S, weight offloading) for niches where vLLM is cost-dominated.

Output format: Artifact `survey/alternative-stacks.md`; 1 hypothesis if a credible beat-vLLM niche exists; findings post.

Sources: llama.cpp, TensorRT-LLM, Modal/Fireworks/Replicate pricing pages, academic edge inference surveys.

Boundaries: Lower priority than GPU-serving angles; be honest if no beat path exists. No code.
resultMd: Delivered `survey/alternative-stacks.md` (sar_6XU4Dsb_mvhn). CPU llama.cpp/edge and managed per-token APIs do not beat vLLM* at default 512/128 high-goodput; serverless per-second GPU + L40S baseline can beat over-provisioned always-on monoliths when peak:avg ~5–10× (Modal economics). Proposed sh_ARBATA9U5VwO (scale-to-zero burst + reserved vLLM*, parent sh_lphBfIh_oTE2) with scope caveat vs fully utilized vLLM*. Findings: sp_y6osYsXStkfE.
